detail.summary:
Both independent deliverables are complete. 

Wrote:
- out/sum.txt = 44 (sum of all integers in data/a.txt: 17 + (-4) + 23 + 8)
- out/words.txt = Apple, apple, fig, pear, plum (5 unique words from data/b.txt, case-sensitive ASCII/dictionary order, one per line)
- out/notes.txt = one line: "Sum of all integers in data/a.txt is 44; data/b.txt has 5 unique words."

Commands actually run:
- awk '{s+=$1} END{print s}' data/a.txt > out/sum.txt
- LC_ALL=C sort -u <(tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' < data/b.txt | sed '/^$/d') > out/words.txt
- printf '...%s...%s...' "$(cat out/sum.txt)" "$(wc -l < out/words.txt)" > out/notes.txt
- cat out/sum.txt, cat out/words.txt, cat out/notes.txt for verification
- Cross-check: python3 -c "print(sum(int(l) for l in open('data/a.txt')))" -> 44

Note: I initially used plain `sort -u`, which under the ambient locale produced "apple" before "Apple". I re-ran with LC_ALL=C to enforce true case-sensitive ordering (uppercase 'A' first), which is what the task requires.
evidence: out/sum.txt contains 44; python3 manual sum also 44
out/words.txt has 5 lines: Apple, apple, fig, pear, plum (LC_ALL=C sort -u)
out/notes.txt single line stating sum 44 and 5 unique words
